notes: Top-level project/job rows receive workspaceKey=WORKSPACE; child rows use parentId for ParentIdIndex.

Target schema for both console-first creation and the optional full-stack CloudFormation/SAM template. Top-level project/job rows receive workspaceKey=WORKSPACE; child rows use parentId for ParentIdIndex.

tables.name: TeamFollowUp-Activity
notes: Activity events use itemId as the partition key and activityKey = ISO timestamp + # + unique eventId as the sort key.
Item-scoped history uses Query on the composite primary key. Application-wide history scans the table because no activity GSI was created.
Target schema for both deployment paths. Item-scoped history queries itemId; app-wide history scans this table because it has no GSI.

tables.name: TeamFollowUp-Users
notes: The small six-member user table stores Cognito subject mappings in cognitoSub; Lambda scans it because no Cognito-subject GSI exists.
Target schema for both deployment paths. Cognito subject lookup scans the small six-member table because no cognitoSub GSI is defined.

tables.name: TeamFollowUp-Archive
notes: Archived records preserve the original item ID, parent/root relationships, content and timestamps.
Activity events remain in TeamFollowUp-Activity and retain item-specific histories after a subtree is archived.
Restore validates parent/child hierarchy before moving selected records back to TeamFollowUp-Items.
Target schema for both deployment paths. Archive rows preserve the original item ID, hierarchy and timestamps.

The tables array is the target physical DynamoDB contract for both the primary AWS Console deployment and the optional full-stack CloudFormation/SAM automation template. This JSON is a reference and test input; it does not provision resources.

backend/template.yaml creates all four tables and indexes from scratch; it does not accept table-name parameters or assume existing tables. The default ResourceNamePrefix produces the same TeamFollowUp-Items, TeamFollowUp-Activity, TeamFollowUp-Users, and TeamFollowUp-Archive names used in the console procedure.

The template creates the Cognito pool and public app client, the four DynamoDB tables, Amplify Hosting app/branch, API Gateway HTTP API, Lambda and scoped IAM, CloudWatch logs/dashboard/alarms, and a $1 monthly budget with actual/forecast email alerts. It is an automation reference, not the primary deployment method.
The handler uses the physical Items/Archive indexes listed here. It scans the small Users table for cognitoSub and scans Activity for application-wide history because neither table has a GSI.

Activity's itemId + activityKey primary key is authoritative; eventId is a regular attribute. The frontend has no local database/demo adapter; application data goes through the Cognito-authenticated API.

DynamoDB data tables use CloudFormation DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy Retain in the automation template. Deleting the stack therefore retains table data; the retained tables must be handled before recreating a stack with the same names.

currentConsoleBootstrap.compatibilityWarning: The console-created Cognito pool/client and four tables recorded below are the actual state of the user's current AWS account as operator-reported; this historical inventory does not constrain the target architecture or template. For a fresh environment, the optional template creates a new Cognito pool/client and all four DynamoDB tables with matching keys and indexes. Do not deploy the full-stack template into the same account/Region while the console-created resources with the same physical names still exist; CloudFormation will not automatically adopt them. The current application uses direct Cognito SRP sign-in, so a Cognito managed-login domain and hosted-UI callback URLs are not required.
